column6: The thesis quantifies over f in A_* and g in B_* (normal functionals); ours over arbitrary linear functionals f, g. Harmless generalisation: normality of f and g is never used, only ultraweak continuity of the two candidate extensions. The thesis states this embedded uniqueness claim without proof.
Definition only: the map gamma(f,g) = (f(x)g(y)) of part 1.

Part 2. 'Orthonormal basis' is rendered as orthonormal + dense span, whereas cstar.tex (the Definition preceding `orthonormal`) defines it as a MAXIMAL orthonormal set. The two are equivalent and the thesis itself uses the equivalence (109V: 'to see that G is maximal it suffices to show that the span of G is dense'), but the equivalence is not proved in this module.

Part 3 (existence). The exercise's route is parts 1 and 2 plus the existence of orthonormal bases; ours instead takes the completion of the algebraic tensor product H (x) K with Mathlib's inner product, so neither l2_tensor nor orthonormal_basis_iff_l2_iso is used.

Part 1 makes three claims; the statement carries two (Omega is order separating; every np-functional on T is an operator-norm limit of finite sums from Omega). The third - that omega -> omega o gamma_odot is a bijection from Omega onto the basic functionals - is only half present, as the unlabelled isBasicFunctional_comp_lift and exists_conjProdNP_of_isBasicFunctional; the uniqueness half ('for some UNIQUE omega in Omega') is stated nowhere in the module. Proof: order separation comes from 30X plus the ultrastrong approximation of 74VI, not from vn-center-separating-fundamental as the exercise directs.

The thesis renormalises Omega to its unital members Omega_1 and quotes 21VII order-separating-norm; ours applies the order separation of Omega directly at gamma_odot(s)*gamma_odot(s) <= ‖s‖^2 . 1, i.e. 21VII's own argument without the renormalisation (which is unavailable when omega(1) = 0).
Part 3's first claim, ‖f o gamma_odot‖ <= ‖f‖, is not in this statement; it is the reverse direction of tensor_basic_4.

Exercise, no printed proof. Its index entry points at Schur's product theorem; our proof needs no Schur - multiplicativity and involution preservation collapse the double sum to x* x.

The exercise asks for a three-way equivalence: (1) beta is cp, (2) M_N beta is cp for each N, (3) (M_N beta)(A,B) >= 0 for positive A, B. The statement proves only (1) <-> (3). Clause (2) appears nowhere in the module; the doc comment says it is subsumed by applying the statement to M_N beta, but that instance is never formed.
The exercise's corollary. beta' is supplied with its defining equation rather than built as a composite.
beta_gamma is rendered as an arbitrary ultraweakly continuous g with g o gamma = beta, which is the same map by 112XI's uniqueness.

The printed proof's inequality beta_odot(s)* beta_odot(s) <= ‖f‖‖g‖ beta_odot(s* s), but derived without amplifying f: cp-cs is applied to a vector of arguments and the difference is split as P(x)R' + R(x)P' + R(x)R'. This replaces the thesis's M_n f and M_n (x) bookkeeping.
